fields.description:
## Context

A 200 from `/health` does not establish that this container can serve an MCP request, yet it is
all the blue-green cutover waits for. `/health` is a FastMCP `custom_route` registered
deliberately OUTSIDE the auth middleware and the DNS-rebinding guard (`src/rebar/_mcp_health.py`,
`register_health_route`), and `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` polls
`GET http://127.0.0.1:<newport>/health` until 200 and flips the nginx upstream — the deploy path
never issues one `/mcp` request. Measured on the box 2026-08-28, a container was promoted 54 s
before it served its first `/mcp` request. A container whose
`REBAR_MCP_HTTP_ALLOWED_HOSTS` does not admit the hostname real traffic carries answers `/health`
200 while 421-ing every real request, and the deploy promotes it — the class of
`mobile-groovy-badger`, which established that `/health` must carry signal enough for the gate to
mean something. Narrative: comments.

## Approach

Drive one real `initialize` through this server's own `StreamableHTTPSessionManager` inside the
ASGI lifespan — after the session manager is running, before Starlette answers
`lifespan.startup.complete` — and publish the outcome as a `handshake` object on `/health`. Uvicorn accepts no connection until lifespan startup completes
(Starlette's `Router.lifespan` sends `lifespan.startup.complete` only after entering that
context), so a later `/health` 200 proves by construction that this container has already served
an MCP handshake. Only that ordering buys the implication, so this is no background task or lazy
field.

**Conclusive.** The probe calls `mcp.session_manager.handle_request(scope, receive, send)` — the
entry point the `/mcp` route serves through (`StreamableHTTPASGIApp(self._session_manager)`,
`mcp/server/fastmcp/server.py:970`). A 200 cannot be produced unless the guard admitted the Host,
`StreamableHTTPServerTransport` parsed the body, the session manager started a server task, and
`Server.run` answered the `initialize` request. A throwaway in-process probe
against a `FastMCP` built as `build_server` builds it returned 200 in 3.0 ms with an admitting
allowlist and 421 "Invalid Host header" in 2.1 ms with a non-admitting one. Boundary: calling the
session manager directly does not traverse `RequireAuthMiddleware`/`ProxyAuthMiddleware` (the
server holds no credential to present to itself). That is deliberate, and is why an auth-enabled
boot is UNAFFECTED: it reports the same truthful transport-path result (pinned by an AC below), so
the gate cannot freeze an auth-enabled deployment. The handshake proves the transport + protocol
path, not auth config.

**Bounded.** The drive runs under `anyio.fail_after(budget)` with module constant
`DEFAULT_HANDSHAKE_BUDGET_SECONDS = 10`, wrapped so a `TimeoutError`, any `Exception`, or a
non-200 status becomes a reported failure record rather than a raise; boot continues. The timeout
scope and clock are injected parameters — the seam `drain_then_exit(..., sleep=, monotonic=)`
already uses here — so the bound is provable with a fake clock, not by sleeping.

**Probe Host** (`select_probe_host`) is a total function of this server's
`TransportSecuritySettings` and bind: (1) the first `allowed_hosts` entry that is a literal host
(no `*`) — on the box `rebar.solutions.navateam.com` (`infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:359`),
what real traffic carries; (2) else the first `host:*` entry materialized as `host:<bind port>`,
the form `_validate_host` matches (`mcp/server/transport_security.py`); (3) else the bind address, `0.0.0.0`/`::` -> `127.0.0.1`. An allowlist admitting nothing usable — empty, or only
unsupported wildcard forms like `*.example.com`, which `_validate_host` never matches — falls to
(3) and is refused 421 by its own guard: the AC-2 case. Allowlist-first, not bind-first, is
deliberate: the box binds `0.0.0.0:8091` and admits only the public hostname, so a bind-addressed
probe would report a correct production container as failed.

The deploy gate closes like the store gate (`autodeploy.sh` 5b): after `/health` 200, refuse the
upstream flip when `handshake.ok` is present and false; an absent field promotes (mixed-version
safety, as the `store` gate treats an older container). The refusal calls
`record_mcp_backoff_failure`, NOT the `record_backoff_failure` 5b uses: `$BACKOFF_FILE` gates the
whole script, so recording there would let an mcp failure suppress the review-bot deploy
(`autodeploy.sh:64-69`). 5b's own wrong recorder is a separate pre-existing defect, filed as
`prespinal-gem-kinkajou`.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_mcp_health.py` — `select_probe_host`, the ASGI `initialize` drive, the bounded
  never-raising `run_startup_handshake`, `install_startup_handshake` (wraps
  `app.router.lifespan_context`, unwrapping any `ProxyAuthMiddleware`), the `handshake` field on
  `/health`, and its call from `run_http_with_grace`. 463 LOC today, staying under the 800 cap.
- `tests/unit/test_mcp_health_startup_handshake.py` — the unit tests.
- `tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_http_transport.py` — pin the `/health` `handshake` key.
- `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` — readiness gate on `handshake.ok`.
- `tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py` — deploy-gate tests on the existing `mcp_box`
  harness, which stubs per-port `/health` bodies.

No new config key: the budget is a module constant, for the reason the docstring records for
`DEFAULT_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECONDS`.

## Testing

Every assertion is anchored: each test first proves the handshake actually RAN (a drive counter,
or the record's presence) and only then asserts its outcome — an assertion that passes when the
handshake never ran is this bug restated. Both directions are covered, the bound is proved with an
injected clock rather than a sleep, and each production edit is reverted individually with its
targeted test required to fail (rc checked).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A correctly configured server reports a successful startup handshake on `/health`:
      `test_correctly_configured_server_reports_a_successful_handshake` asserts the drive counter
      incremented and the record is `{"ok": True, "status": 200}`.
- [ ] A server whose host allowlist does not admit its own probe reports the handshake as failed
      with the refusing status instead of reporting ready:
      `test_unadmitted_probe_host_is_reported_as_failed_with_421` asserts `ok is False`,
      `status == 421`.
- [ ] A handshake that exceeds its budget is reported as a failure and boot continues:
      `test_a_hanging_drive_is_bounded_by_the_budget` (injected clock, no sleep) asserts the call
      returns a failure record naming the timeout.
- [ ] A handshake whose drive raises never propagates the exception:
      `test_a_raising_drive_is_reported_not_propagated` asserts the record carries the message and
      the lifespan still yields.
- [ ] The handshake completes inside the ASGI lifespan before uvicorn accepts its first
      connection: `test_handshake_is_recorded_before_lifespan_startup_complete` drives the raw
      lifespan protocol and asserts the record exists before `lifespan.startup.complete`.
- [ ] An auth-enabled server still reports a successful handshake, so the gate cannot freeze its
      deploys: `test_an_auth_enabled_server_still_reports_a_successful_handshake` asserts `ok is
      True` with a token verifier configured.
- [ ] The blue-green cutover refuses to promote a container reporting a failed handshake:
      `test_failed_handshake_container_is_not_promoted` asserts `mcp-handshake-failed` logged, the
      upstream include byte-identical, nginx not reloaded, the container removed.
- [ ] A container whose `/health` predates the field is still promoted (mixed-version safety):
      `test_container_with_no_handshake_field_still_promotes` asserts the upstream flips.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and the affected test modules exit 0 in-session.
- [ ] Each production edit reverted individually makes its targeted test fail (rc checked).
